now: The hunt's fight is visible: `encounter` steps `battle.stepper` one turn every `config.turnSteps` sim steps, emits a `battle:strike` per blow, calls the move out over the trainer and the wild, and a fainted lead is replaced mid-duel rather than ending it. A wiped party pays a tenth of the wallet and is taken to the Pokemon Center. Ether and Max Ether exist, a Potion no longer revives, and one ball per defeated wild is a named rule (DECISIONS #72). The production build now carries its sprite art and the gate asserts it, and exactly one thing runs the hunt at a time - visible is `encounter`, hidden is `idle`, and the encounter counter changes hands at the edge. A hunt walks a circuit that visits the places the biome composes, steps off it to reach the creature standing on a slot, and fights it there; there is one route and the showcases walk it too. Nothing appears from nowhere any more: the tall-grass step roll is deleted everywhere and the city spawns nothing. Every species has its own drop table, derived from its typing and rarity and mirrored against the evolution bill; loot lands in a Stash and consumables in a Bag, two views of one Map with a Sell-Lock the automation obeys and the counter does not; and a run opens with FIELD_START_MONEY that is deliberately not 'earned'. Auto-Heal, Auto-Revive, Auto-Ether and Auto-Lead decide inside the fight from pure rules the fold runs too. and a panel configures all ten of them - the healing ladder edited in place, rules reordered with buttons. and every move is drawn as its own element and delivery. The brief is implemented end to end; and the effects are photographable at any element and hour through `?showcase=encounter&mode=vfx-*`, with two of them under the regress matrix - targeting, the stash/bag split and per-species loot, the five missing automations, and the move VFX - are not started.

baseline.note: demo city at noon. Real numbers, but the scene has no buildings, no NPCs and no characters yet.

open.what: `openDuel`'s `nextAlly` still swaps in **party order**, not by matchup. `between` is wired for real (DECISIONS #76) and `automation.chooseLead` is asked at engagement, but a member that faints mid-fight is replaced by whoever is next in line rather than by whoever can win — so the brief's lead rule holds when a fight starts and not when one turns.

`useItem()` still has zero consumers. The duel applies items through `battle.applyAction` on a combatant record, not on a `pokemon` instance, so the intent object it returns has no caller and the manual-use path is still unbuilt.
The coast circuit runs through inland grass rather than along the shoreline -- the bend heuristic prefers path/tallgrass, and the shore is neither.
`go()` is serialised but not cancellable: once a scene starts building, the player waits for it.
Travelling mid-encounter calls `encounter.cancel()` with no prompt. A silent loss of a fight the player was in.
Accuracy and evasion stages are not modelled -- deliberate, and stated at `stats.js:41`. Only the five battle stats stage.

Daylight frames have no motivated light source, which is what four rounds of blind A/B judging lost on every time. Night and cave frames, which have practicals, win. See `docs/STATUS-ARCHIVE.json` -> gate.blindJudging.

`pacing.js MEASURED` still projects the income model DECISIONS #69 deleted, and now also predates per-species drop tables and the ₽100,000 opening purse. The header (`pacing.js:22`) says the table is stale; it is staler.
